Spanning Local Tornaments in Locally Sicomplete Digraphs Abstract We investigate the existance of a spanning local tornament with possibly high connectivity inn a highly connected localy sicomplete digraph.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the existence of a k-connected spanning subgraph H of a given digraph D with a given connectivity k, where H is a spanning local tournament, a spanning semicomplete tournament, or a spanning semicompletion.
the existence of a local tournament in a digraph with certain properties.
the following question: Given a highly connected locally (semi-)complete digraph G, what is the maximum number of vertices in a spanning (semi-)local tournament of G?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
every (3 k − 2)- connected locally semicompleted digraph has a spanning k-connected local tournament, for every k ≥ 1.
every k-connected locally semicomplete (or semicomplete) digraph contains a spanning k-connected local tournament (respectively, a spanning k-connected tournament).
every k-connected locally semicomplete (semicomplete) digraph contains a spanning k-connected local (semicomplete, respectively) tournament.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
for every k ≥ 2, every (3k−2)-connected locally (k+1)-semicomplete digraph G contains a spanning k-connected locally (k+2)-semicomplete subdigraph H such that G − V(H) is (k − 2, k)-semicomplete.
every locally semicomplete (resp., semicomplete) digraph of connectivity k (resp., k ≥ 2) contains a k-connected local (resp., spanning) tournament.
every locally semicomplete graph with sufficiently high connectivity has a spanning local tournament of the highest possible connectivity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the existence of local tournaments is a robust property in the sense that the local tournament can be chosen to have high connectivity and the host graph can have low connectivity.
the local structure of a locally semicomplete tournament plays a key role in the construction of a spanning local digraph with a given connectivity.
we can obtain a spanning local tournament of high connectivity by using only the connectivity of the digraph.
